analysis: Reviewed the supplied units of provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift. The only changes are test additions at head lines ~3140-3240, shown in the patch excerpt: remembersHeaderVerdictsOnlyForUnchangedFiles and replacedLookalikeIsReadAgain for SSDWholeRootMaintainer, which caches header-ownership verdicts. The tests assert that a file whose header is corrupted after an earlier pass (same size and mtime, ctime changed) loses its ownership proof and is not deleted or counted, and that a lookalike later replaced by a real block is re-read. These are test-only changes with no production code exposure. Related threat model T-041 (at-rest SSD cache, HMAC names, TTL/LRU) and TB-003 are unchanged by the tests; the tests pin fail-safe behavior (no deletion of unowned files). The head_text unit shown is the file beginning (lines 1-609) and the base unit is the sidecar tail (4238-4588). Neither contains the changed hunk beyond the truncated patch excerpt, so the production SSDWholeRootMaintainer verdict cache (not supplied here) is unverified. If the production maintainer change uses ctime or an equivalent change marker, as the test implies, the security posture (no deletion of foreign files) is preserved. That implementation lives in another batch and should be examined there. No regression is identified from these units.
